::: {.callout-note title="Retrospective case study" icon=false}
Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains
no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from
the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.
:::

## Observation

- SPY fell 1.54% and QQQ 2.04%. NVDA fell 3.55%.
- Crude oil rose 6.6% to $84.46. XOM gained 2.4% and the commodity group was the only one clearly positive.
- Long Treasuries fell too: TLT lost 1.65%. The VIX rose 13.5% to 20.7.
- The weakest groups were space (-6.4%), semiconductors (-4.2%) and cyclicals (-3.2%, with CAT -6.9%).

## Mechanism

**Channel: the risk-free rate, with a cash-flow effect on cyclicals.**

- An Iranian missile attack on US forces raised the risk of lost oil supply.
- Oil jumped, which raised expected inflation on the day of a Federal Reserve decision.
- Higher expected inflation raised the odds of rate increases, so bond prices fell and yields rose.
- A higher discount rate hit the longest-duration equities hardest: space and semiconductors.
- Higher fuel and input costs hit cyclicals through their margins.

The signature of an inflation shock is that stocks and bonds fall on the same day. In a growth scare, bonds would have rallied.

## What happened next

Over the following five trading days SPY rose 5.5%, NVDA 15.4% and MSFT 24.8%. Oil eased, and Microsoft's results after that day's close changed the subject.

## Lesson

An oil supply shock can be identified from three things moving together: energy up, bonds down, cyclicals down. It can also fade within days if no supply is actually lost. Before extrapolating a geopolitical move, check whether barrels have been removed from the market or only the fear of it.
